description:
Repository convention memory. In this account the speaker of user messages is a code repository (its peer). Those messages relay a ticket, human comments, code review findings and CI results for work in that repository.
Capture durable, reusable knowledge about how work must be done in this repository: coding conventions, design-system rules, required checks or commands before pushing, review expectations, recurring reviewer findings and how they were resolved, and tooling or deployment constraints.
Record a convention only when a message states or demonstrates it as a rule for the repository: a reviewer flags it, a human corrects the work, or CI enforces it. Do not record requirements that apply only to the current ticket.
Ignore ticket acceptance criteria, one-off instructions, CI progress notices, bot boilerplate and anything the assistant says about itself.
Store each convention area as a separate memory; do not mix unrelated areas.

fields.name: topic
fields.description:
Convention area, lowercase with underscores, at most 3 words, for example styling_tokens, pre_push_checks, review_expectations, test_coverage, commit_messages.
The topic is an identity component together with user. Merge only true aliases for the same convention area; related areas stay separate.

fields.name: content
fields.description:
Markdown bullets, one per distinct rule: the rule, where it applies (paths, packages, layers), and the reason or source (reviewer finding, human correction, CI check) when given.
Write each rule so an agent working on a different ticket in this repository can follow it. Omit ticket IDs, PR numbers, dates and details that only matter for one change.
Example:
- Use semantic design tokens for colors and spacing in frontend components; hardcoded rem or hex values are flagged in review.
